jobs.title: Technical Consulting Director, Site Investigation and Remediation
jobs.description:
Lead Complex Remediation Projects That Shape Environmental Outcomes

At ERM
, we are seeking a Technical Director, Site Investigation and Remediation (SIR)
to join our growing team in Indianapolis, IN
. This is a strategic leadership opportunity for an accomplished environmental professional who is passionate about solving complex site investigation and remediation challenges, developing innovative technical solutions, and building lasting client relationships. As a senior leader within a global consulting organization, you will help guide major remediation programs, influence technical strategy, mentor emerging talent, and contribute to the continued growth of ERM’s Site Investigation and Remediation practice both regionally and nationally.

Why This Role Matters

Environmental challenges are becoming increasingly complex, requiring innovative thinking, technical excellence, and strong leadership. In this role, you will serve as a trusted advisor to clients navigating complex regulatory and technical issues while helping deliver sustainable remediation solutions that protect communities and support responsible development. Your expertise will directly influence project success, client outcomes, and the growth of ERM’s Site Investigation and Remediation (SIR) practice.

What Your Impact Is

As a Technical Director, you will leverage your technical expertise, industry relationships, and consulting experience to deliver high-value solutions for clients across the chemical, manufacturing, oil and gas, power, and other industrial sectors. You will play a key role in advancing remediation strategies, driving business growth, fostering client partnerships, and collaborating with ERM's regional and national technical experts to share leading practices and innovative approaches across the industry.

Required

What You'll Bring

Bachelor's Degree and Advanced Degree in Engineering, Geology, Hydrogeology, or related engineering or science field.
8+ years of consulting experience working with significant industrial clients on complex site investigation/remediation and construction projects under a variety of state, federal, and international regulatory structures.
Expertise in Site Investigation and Remediation (SIR)-related topics, including thought leadership at conferences and/or publications through journals.
Experience guiding a team through all steps of an investigation and remediation design project.
Experience preparing detailed technical and environmental reports.
Experience interacting with regulators and clients to facilitate project progress.
Excellent writing, communication, strategic thinking, and relationship-building skills.
Up-to-date Health and Safety training, including HAZWOPER 40-hour training and OSHA 30-hour training.
Driver's License Required: This position requires a valid driver's license and/or the ability to operate a company vehicle due to the nature of job duties, which include frequent travel to various client locations across a large geographical area.

Preferred

15+ years of consulting experience working with significant industrial clients on complex site investigation/remediation and construction projects.
Recognized technical leadership and industry presence through publications, presentations, conferences, or other professional contributions.
Demonstrated success managing large-scale remediation programs and leading multidisciplinary technical teams.

Key Responsibilities

Serve as a Subject Matter Expert (SME) related to site investigation, remediation, and related engineering on a variety of projects and programs, including those governed by CERCLA (Superfund), RCRA, and State Voluntary Program regulations.
Negotiations and engagement with US EPA and state regulators to coordinate, plan, and implement project strategies within the appropriate regulatory frameworks.
Oversee, manage, and provide technical expertise on site investigation and remediation projects for a variety of clients with complex technical and regulatory issues in the chemical, manufacturing, oil and gas, power, and other industrial sectors.
Design and negotiate remedial solutions for contaminated soil, groundwater, vapor, and sediment, utilizing innovative and emerging remedial treatment technologies as well as traditional systems.
Assist clients in developing and implementing contaminated site management strategies.
Appropriately delegate project assignments to project teams and mentor junior staff.
Develop and expand client relationships that generate repeat business to grow the Site Investigation and Remediation (SIR) practice across the chemical, oil and gas, and manufacturing sectors.
Prepare technical proposals and participate in business development efforts with existing clients and identified leads.
Build strong collaborative relationships with other ERM employees.

Who We Are

As the largest global pure play sustainability consultancy, we partner with the world’s leading organizations, creating innovative solutions to sustainability challenges and unlocking commercial opportunities that meet the needs of today while preserving opportunity for future generations.

At ERM we know that creating a diverse, equitable and inclusive work environment is an essential part of making our company a great place to build a career. We also see our diversity as a strength that helps us create better solutions for our clients. Our diverse team of world-class experts supports clients across the breadth of their organizations to operationalize sustainability, underpinned by our deep technical expertise in addressing their environmental, health, safety, risk and social issues. We call this capability our “boots to boardroom” approach for its comprehensive service model that allows ERM to develop strategic and technical solutions that advance objectives on the ground or at the executive level.

Please submit your resume and brief cover letter.

ERM does not accept recruiting agency resumes. Please do not forward resumes to our jobs alias, ERM employees or any other company location. ERM is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes.

ERM is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based upon race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics.

Thank you for your interest in ERM!

jobs.title: Environmental Compliance Manager (Field Based)
jobs.description:
ERM
is hiring an Environmental Compliance Manager (Owner Advisor)
in Houston, TX
to serve as a trusted partner to our key pharmaceutical client’s project leadership and delivery teams, supporting environmental stewardship and regulatory compliance across a large, fast‑paced capital project. Acting on behalf of the client, this role provides owner‑side environmental leadership across Construction Management (CM), design‑build teams, and contractors, ensuring environmental risks are anticipated, controls are implemented effectively, and compliance obligations are consistently met through a combination of visible field presence and strong leadership influence. This is a Full‑Time (40+ hours per week) limited‑term role with a duration of one (1) year, with potential to extend
.

Responsibilities

Provide owner‑side environmental compliance leadership across the project, ensuring alignment with applicable local, state, and federal requirements and client expectations.
Establish and maintain a clear, project‑specific environmental compliance framework that defines requirements, roles, and interfaces to guide CM and contractor execution.
Maintain strong field presence to validate that environmental controls, practices, and behaviors align with approved plans and permit obligations.
Perform quality checks of contractor and CM environmental inspections and documentation, confirming inspections are occurring at the appropriate cadence and are effective.
Coach CM and contractor teams on environmental findings, gaps, and emerging risks, driving timely and sustainable corrective actions without direct authority.
Identify, assess, and prioritize environmental risks through regulatory aspect and gap reviews, recommending risk‑based mitigation strategies.
Support development, review, and continuous improvement of project environmental plans and procedures to ensure they are executable and field‑ready.
Partner with client environmental SMEs and permitting resources to ensure construction activities remain aligned with permit conditions and reporting expectations.
Develop, track, and communicate environmental performance metrics, trends, and key risks to project and executive leadership.
Participate in environmental incident and spill investigations, ensuring appropriate containment, root cause identification, and preventive actions.
Coordinate with waste vendors and site teams to support compliant waste handling, profiling, storage, and disposal practices.
Support chemical inventory management and applicable regulatory reporting by ensuring data accuracy and clear ownership for updates.
Serve as a primary point of contact for environmental questions requiring practical judgment related to changing scope, sequencing, or site conditions.
Support environmental readiness for startup and commissioning by verifying environmental requirements are integrated into transition plans.

Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Environmental Science, or equivalent experience.
Minimum of 8 years of environmental experience, including significant experience supporting large construction or capital projects.
Demonstrated ability to operate as an owner‑side environmental leader, balancing field verification with programmatic oversight.
Strong working knowledge of construction‑phase environmental compliance domains such as stormwater, spill prevention, waste management, air and dust controls.
Proven ability to translate environmental requirements into practical execution through others.
Experience influencing CM and contractor performance and driving accountability without direct line authority.
Strong communication skills, including the ability to deliver concise, executive‑level updates using metrics and risk‑based insights.
Experience conducting environmental audits or assessments and verifying effective corrective action closure.
High standards for documentation quality, data integrity, and compliance reporting.
Experience in life sciences, pharmaceutical, or similarly regulated industries preferred.
Familiarity with environmental management system concepts and continuous improvement practices preferred.

Who We Are

As the largest global pure play sustainability consultancy, we partner with the world’s leading organizations, creating innovative solutions to sustainability challenges and unlocking commercial opportunities that meet the needs of today while preserving opportunity for future generations.

We also see our diversity as a strength that helps us create better solutions for our clients. Our diverse team of world-class experts supports clients across the breadth of their organizations to operationalize sustainability, underpinned by our deep technical expertise in addressing their environmental, health, safety, risk and social issues. We call this capability our “boots to boardroom” approach for its comprehensive service model that allows ERM to develop strategic and technical solutions that advance objectives on the ground or at the executive level.

will lead the development and delivery of innovative client solutions that strengthen compliance, reduce risk, improve operational performance, and support broader sustainability commitments. within a hybrid and flexible working environment.

Lead client relationship development, sales, and delivery of the full spectrum of ERM’s consulting services, with particular emphasis on growing Sustainable Operations offerings.
Develop and implement EHS compliance and risk management systems that help clients strengthen governance, improve performance, and manage regulatory obligations.
Advise clients on data management, reporting, and disclosure support related to EHS performance.
Develop commercial strategies to pursue and win new business opportunities that drive revenue growth with target clients aligned to ERM’s global strategy.
Listen carefully to client needs and co-develop practical, innovative solutions that deliver long-term value.
Build, grow, and lead a high-performing team, mentoring consultants and helping emerging leaders expand their responsibilities and impact.
Drive service innovation and collaboration across ERM service lines and participate actively in local and regional commercial initiatives.
Expand the visibility of ERM’s Sustainable Operations services through thought leadership, industry engagement, and strategic partnerships.

Drive profitable growth by expanding key client relationships and winning new work across the Sustainable Operations portfolio.
Shape commercial strategy in alignment with ERM’s focus on the world’s leading organizations and priority sectors.
Contribute to the strategic direction of the business as an equity Partner and visible leader within the firm.
Strengthen ERM’s market position by extending client reach, industry relationships, and brand visibility in environmental compliance.

Technical Leadership

Provide strategic and technical leadership in environmental compliance, operational risk, and EHS performance improvement.
Develop and deploy innovative compliance and risk management solutions tailored to complex regulatory environments.
Guide clients in integrating sustainability objectives with compliance, biodiversity, and resource management requirements.
Deliver solutions that improve operational efficiency, reduce risk exposure, and support safe, sustainable, and compliant performance.

Build and lead a high-performing consulting team, creating an environment of accountability, collaboration, and innovation.

Foster a culture that reflects ERM’s commitment to safety, sustainability, inclusion, and high-quality client service.

15+ years of relevant experience in EHS compliance, environmental compliance, and risk management.
Executive-level consulting or corporate leadership experience with a strong track record of business development and client growth.

Broad solutions experience spanning compliance, reporting, and operational risk.
Strong communicator, collaborator, and people leader with the ability to mentor and grow high-performing teams.
Established client network or market credibility in sectors such as technology, energy, or other industrial markets is preferred.

Success Factors

Entrepreneurial mindset with the vision to grow a practice and expand market impact.
Strong executive presence, communication skills, and ability to influence internal and external stakeholders.
Credibility in environmental compliance with an integrated view of sustainability and operational performance.
Commercial acumen, strategic thinking, and a collaborative approach to leadership.
Passion for developing people, advancing innovation, and contributing to ERM’s long-term success as a Partner.

For the  Consulting Partner, EHS & Sustainable Operations
position, the anticipated annual base pay is  $171,000 - $217,000 (USD)

This role may be eligible for bonus pay subject to the sole discretion of ERM and its policies and procedures (casual and fixed term/flex force employees are not bonus eligible).

Class A Van Driver (OTR)

Drive established OTR routes across North America while supporting environmental and industrial services. You’ll transport both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, ensuring each load is moved safely, legally, and in line with customer and site requirements. This is a safety-first role where attention to detail directly impacts compliance and continuity of critical work.

You’ll complete DOT-compliant inspections
, verify safety equipment and load conditions, and follow required procedures for hazardous materials handling. Accurate logkeeping

Day to day, you’ll coordinate with dispatch

Responsible for transporting both hazardous and non-hazardous materials between customer locations and facility sites using Class A equipment. You’ll ensure every trip is completed with a strong safety mindset, following environmental and DOT requirements while protecting people, property, and the surrounding community.

Your Day-to-day Work Includes

Performing safe loading and unloading procedures, verifying materials and securing loads correctly.
Completing DOT-compliant pre-trip, post-trip, and along-the-route inspections, escalating any safety concerns as needed.
Maintaining accurate records and logs in line with regulatory expectations.
Adhering to strict spill prevention, waste-handling, and disposal protocols throughout transportation.
Supporting a team culture grounded in integrity, communication, and sustainability.

This role is ideal for a reliable CDL Class A driver who understands regulatory compliance, prioritizes hazard awareness, and takes pride in careful, detail-driven work.
